spec_issues: The prompt says 'Optimize for describing every real change without claiming anything the screenshots don't show'. The metric scores only recall: the judge marks each reference observation supported, contradicted or missing (tests/task/validate.py:43-48), and extra or hallucinated claims cost nothing unless they contradict a reference. DeepSeek 4myy8p worked this out ('extra candidate claims not penalized').

The review rule for this task explicitly allows using a specialist model as a labelling tool (tests/task/review.py:39-41). Every top run distilled a frontier VLM teacher through OpenRouter: Fable dlcubp claude-sonnet-5.5, Opus fqi4zj claude-opus-5.5, Opus 1v1zlc gpt-6-luna (the judge model itself).
verifier_issues: **The floor sits below a blind baseline.** One fixed paragraph listing common UI changes, sent for every pair without looking at the images, scores 0.3199 raw, i.e. 32.0 on the published scale. The operator measured this and chose not to raise the floor above it: tests/task/task.yaml:44-47 ('Operator decision (2026-09-27): the floor is not raised to the best input-blind description, which scores 0.3199'; tests/task/pipeline/baseline_results.json). Only 3 of the 18 trials clearly beat that paragraph: Fable dlcubp 46.4, Opus fqi4zj 38.0 and Opus 1v1zlc 34.4. Fable 39iyxm (31.1) ties it. The other 14, including every Argon, Astra, Muse and DeepSeek run, score below a constant string.

The held-out set is 14 pairs x 5 rounds, judged by gpt-6-luna (tests/config.json). Judge noise alone moves the same blind paragraph between 0.280 and 0.378 per round (baseline_results.json). Pair sampling noise on 14 pairs is larger still.

The throughput gate is strict: 70 requests at concurrency 14 must finish in 14 s or the run scores zero (frontier_ml/runtime/resources.py:638-662; tests/task/validate.py:37). Selfcheck hosts vary a lot. Muse 3ys4t8 failed all four selfchecks at 17.6-27.6 s, yet its graded batch passed, since it scored nonzero ([363]: 'high host-to-host variance ... identical stack did 70 requests in 9.2s on a rented H100'). Opus fqi4zj's first selfcheck failed at 14.28 s. A near-threshold server can be zeroed or passed by host draw, and the grade page does not report the graded batch time.
task_level.noise: Orderings are erratic: Fable 31.1/23.2/46.4, Opus 26.8/34.4/38.0, Argon 16.3/7.1/22.3, Astra 16.0/15.5/8.2, Muse 13.0/1.6/6.5, DeepSeek 21.5/10.6/10.4. DeepSeek's zero-shot $10 run beats both of its fine-tuned runs. With 14 pairs and judge spread of about +/-0.05, the $10 win (Fable 31.1 vs Opus 26.8) is within noise. The $200 win (Fable 46.4 vs Opus 38.0) and the $50 win (Opus 34.4 vs Fable 23.2) are more robust but not certain.
task_level.elicitation: Two data strategies split the field. Claude runs trained on real GUI video frame pairs (GUI-World, VideoCUA) with a strong frontier teacher and scored highest. Astra used only procedurally generated HTML pairs with labels by construction (no teacher calls: no OpenRouter model ids in 4x2ecc or zdfagx) and scored 8-16. Astra spent 1.2-1.9 h per trial. No harness-specific behaviour (imagegen, sub-agents) was seen. No trial touched the benchmark repo or the HF tasks dataset. DeepSeek toua7h listed /opt/frontier-ml, which is the local agent tool package, not the grader.
task_level.epoch_rationale: No false positives, false negatives or infrastructure zeros change a winner: all 18 reviews passed or were skipped and are consistent with the trajectories, and the strict throughput gate zeroed nobody. The scale is still badly calibrated. Most scores sit below a constant input-blind paragraph (32.0), and the $10 winner is inside judge noise.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: No gaming observed: no trial padded its output with blind enumerations, even though recall-only scoring would reward it, and the 5 pairs/s gate limits long outputs anyway. The measured signal comes almost entirely from distilling frontier VLM teachers onto real GUI frame pairs. On the absolute scale, the benchmark shows that 14 of 18 agent-built models do worse than a fixed paragraph.
